title: Learning Fingerprints for Medical Time Series with Redundancy-Constrained Information Maximization
claim: Standard representations entangle distinct factors into one vector; ours separates them into independent tokens, yielding better accuracy and efficiency.
layout: 2x2 grid: top contrast cartoons, bottom bar charts; watercolor beaker vs. separate jars
description: A 2x2 composite. Top left, titled 'Entangled View (Standard Representation)': an ECG trace feeds a watercolor beaker where blue (Identity), red (Pathology) and grey (Noise) inks swirl together into a 'single holistic vector'. Top right, titled 'Disentangled View (Fingerprint Representation)': an ECG trace with three teal arrows pointing to three separate glass jars holding a DNA helix (Identity), a heart (Pathology) and a noise waveform (Noise). Bottom left is a bar chart of F1 for Ti-MAE, SimMTM and Ours, scratch vs. pre-train. The pre-train gains are annotated: -0.96% and +4.42% for the baselines, and +13.08% for ours, highlighted in blue. Bottom right is a bar chart of average rank per model, with ours at 1.24 in blue. A yellow line gives the inference time ratio on a secondary axis. The eye goes first to the colorful beaker and jars.
caption: Paradigm Shift in MedTS Representation. Unlike standard MAEs that produce variable-length, entangled sequences (Top Left), TS-Fingerprint (Top Right) imposes a division of labor, compressing signals into fixed, disentangled tokens where each slot captures an independent physiological factor. The performance plots (Bottom Left) demonstrate that this disentanglement design is crucial for pre-training, outperforming entangled baselines [ref] by a significant margin. Bottom Right shows the average rank of models across all datasets and metrics (lower is better). The proposed method achieves the best overall performance, attaining an average rank of 1.24 while maintaining fast inference speed (14% faster than Medformer) and consistently outperforming all baseline methods.
abstract: Learning meaningful representations from medical time series (MedTS) such as ECG or EEG signals is a critical challenge. These signals are often high-dimensional, variable-length and rife with noise. Existing self-supervised approaches, such as Masked Autoencoders (MAEs) are highly effective for pre-training general-purpose encoders. However, they do not explicitly learn compact and semantically interpretable latent representations, typically relying on heuristic aggregation strategies such as global average pooling or a designated [CLS] token. We propose a novel framework that compresses a variable-length MedTS into a fixed-size set of $k$ latent Fingerprint Tokens. Our architecture employs a cross-attention bottleneck to generate these tokens and is trained with a dual-objective function. The first objective is a reconstruction loss, which ensures the tokens are \textit{sufficient statistics} for the original data. The second, a diversity penalty based on the Total Coding Rate (TCR), explicitly minimizes the redundancy between tokens, encouraging them to become statistically \textit{disentangled} representations. We present the theoretical justification for our method, framing it as a novel \textbf{Disentangled Rate-Distortion} problem. This approach produces a low-dimensional, interpretable, and sample-efficient representation, where each token is encouraged to capture an independent factor of variation, paving the way for more robust digital biomarkers.
